newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND WINS AGAIN IN BORMIO.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND WINS AGAIN IN BORMIO.

text.p: France's Luc Alphand took his second World Cup Alpine skiing downhill victory of the season on Sunday on a treacherous and icy Bormio piste that got the better of many racers.

Alphand, the World Cup downhill champion for the past two seasons who won in Val Gardena earlier in the month, clocked an unofficial two minutes 00.51 seconds down the 3.2 km track to go further ahead in the downhill standings.
The Frenchman also won in Bormio in 1995.
William Besse was second in 2:00.72 to become the first Swiss men's downhiller to secure a podium finish this season.
Italian Kristian Ghedina, who also won a downhill in Val Gardena this month and who is Alphand's major rival for the World Cup title, was third in 2:01.18.

The icy conditions on the Stelvio piste, bathed treacherously in bright sunlight and deep shadows, took their toll with four of the first eight starters crashing out including Austrian World Cup overall leader Hans Knauss.
The race was held up several times as officials mended safety netting damaged by crashing skiers.
